# Lock service with fencing tokens

Implement `LockService` and `Resource` in `solution.py`, keeping all state in
`runtime.Store` (see `runtime.py`).

```python
LockService(store, ttl: int)
acquire(client: str, now: int) -> int | None
release(client: str, token: int, now: int) -> bool

Resource(store, name: str)
write(token: int, value: str) -> bool
read() -> str | None
```

- `acquire` grants the lock when no one holds an unexpired lease, and returns a fencing
  token. A lease granted at `now` expires at `now + ttl`; it is expired for any
  `now >= now + ttl`. Tokens are integers that strictly increase over the life of the
  store. If `client` already holds the unexpired lease, `acquire` returns that lease's
  token. Otherwise it returns `None`.
- `release` ends the lease if `client` holds the lease with `token` and it is unexpired at
  `now`, and returns whether it did.
- A `Resource` is protected by fencing: `write` rejects (returns `False`, no effect) a
  token that was never issued, or a token lower than one already used for an accepted
  write to that resource. Otherwise it stores `value` and returns `True`.
- Many `LockService` and `Resource` objects in many threads may share one `Store`; all
  `LockService` objects for a store use the same `ttl`. Callers supply `now`, and calls
  from different clients may arrive with out-of-order times.

Use P to model the design before implementing it, and to test the implementation.
`snappea` and the `pysnappea` Python package are installed. Keep your P files and
tests in this directory; the tests must run with `python -m pytest`.
----
---
name: p-modeling
description: Design concurrent or retrying code with a P model checked by snappea, then test the real implementation against what the model found.
---

# P modeling

P finds bugs that only appear in some orderings: two clients read the same version,
a retry arrives after the state changed, a step fails between read and write. Use it
for shared state, retries, concurrency and recovery. Pure transformations need only
ordinary tests.

The model is worth what it changes in the code and tests. Follow these steps in order.
The same steps are built into the CLI: `snappea guide`.

## 1. List the risks (before any code)

Write down, in `DESIGN.md`:

- the contract in checkable sentences ("a retried request returns its first result and
  has no further effect");
- the real atomic primitives (one compare-and-swap on one key, a lock, a transaction).
  Everything else can interleave;
- 5-10 concrete scenarios that could break the contract. Always consider:
  two clients that read the same version; a retry after another request changed the
  state (including retries of rejected or empty results); two objects sharing one
  store; each precondition false on its own; values exactly at each boundary.

## 2. Model the algorithm, not the API

- One machine for the store, holding exactly what the real store holds. Its handlers
  are the real primitives: `load` replies with (version, value); `cas` succeeds only at
  the current version.
- Client machines run your algorithm: send load, receive, decide, send cas, retry on
  failure. Every `send`/`receive` is a point where another client can run. If the
  whole operation is one handler, the model assumes the race away.
- A `spec` monitor computes the expected results from the contract and the history of
  requests, independently of the algorithm, and asserts each actual result.
- Drive it with 2-3 clients and small `choose(n)` inputs, plus fixed tests for the
  scenarios from step 1. Start from the [syntax reference](reference/p-patterns.md)
  and [CAS + retries example](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p).

## 3. Check until it passes for real

```sh
snappea check            # every test case, then coverage and mutation checks
```

- Exit 1 is work to do: a bug (fix the design; keep the scenario), a coverage gap
  (add a scenario), or a surviving mutant (an assertion is missing). Read each one.
- Do not finish with `--no-mutation` or `--allow-incomplete-coverage`. Use them only
  while iterating. If search is incomplete, shrink the bounds or raise `--timeout`.
- A bug found here is the payoff: write it down, fix the design, then implement.

## 4. Implement, then test what the model explored

Read [testing the implementation](guides/testing-implementation.md). For each
scenario and each bug the model found, write a Python test that makes it happen on the
real code. Random thread stress rarely hits a race; force it:

- wrap the store so a competing call runs between this call's load and its
  compare-and-swap, or so two calls read the same version before either writes;
- retry a request after another request changed the state, through a second object.

Add an observation test: run real calls, record their actual arguments and results as
events, and check them against your P spec with `snappea.check_events` (install
`pysnappea`, `import snappea`). See [implementation](guides/implementation.md).

## 5. Prove the tests can fail

Break your implementation on purpose, one change at a time (ignore the
compare-and-swap result, drop a retry memo, flip a boundary `<` to `<=`, keep state
in the object instead of the store). Run the tests each time; every break must fail a
test. Add a test for any that pass. Restore the code.

## Done means

- `snappea check` exits 0, with complete search or stated bounds.
- `python -m pytest` passes, including forced-interleaving and observation tests.
- Every hand-made break from step 5 fails a test.
- `DESIGN.md` states the contract, primitives, scenarios, model bounds, what the model
  found, and what is not covered.

## References

- [Syntax and commands](reference/p-patterns.md), [modeling](guides/modeling.md),
  [scenarios and oracles](guides/scenarios-and-oracles.md), [recovery](guides/recovery.md).
- Examples: [CAS + generated retries](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p),
  [reservation + Python tests](examples/reservation/Reservation.p),
  [generated histories](examples/bounded-history/bounded-history.p),
  [durable retry](examples/durable-retry/DurableRetry.p),
  [versioned publication](examples/versioned-publication/Revalidated.p).

import threading

import pytest
from snappea import check_events

import solution
from runtime import Store
from solution import LockService, Resource

TTL = 2


class HookStore:
    """Store wrapper that runs a callback right after the n-th load of a key."""

    def __init__(self, inner):
        self.inner = inner
        self.loads = {}
        self.hooks = {}  # (key, n) -> callable

    def after_load(self, key, n, fn):
        self.hooks[(key, n)] = fn

    def load(self, key):
        result = self.inner.load(key)
        n = self.loads[key] = self.loads.get(key, 0) + 1
        fn = self.hooks.pop((key, n), None)
        if fn:
            fn()
        return result

    def compare_swap(self, key, version, value):
        return self.inner.compare_swap(key, version, value)


def make():
    store = Store()
    return store, LockService(store, TTL)


# ---- contract and boundaries -------------------------------------------------

def test_basic_acquire_release():
    _, svc = make()
    assert svc.acquire("a", 0) == 1
    assert svc.acquire("b", 1) is None
    assert svc.acquire("a", 1) == 1  # same unexpired lease, same token
    assert svc.release("a", 1, 1) is True
    assert svc.release("a", 1, 1) is False
    assert svc.acquire("b", 1) == 2


def test_expiry_boundary():
    _, svc = make()
    assert svc.acquire("a", 10) == 1
    assert svc.acquire("b", 10 + TTL - 1) is None  # still unexpired
    assert svc.acquire("a", 10 + TTL - 1) == 1
    assert svc.acquire("b", 10 + TTL) == 2  # expired exactly at now + ttl
    assert svc.acquire("a", 10 + TTL) is None


def test_expired_holder_gets_new_token():
    _, svc = make()
    assert svc.acquire("a", 0) == 1
    assert svc.acquire("a", TTL) == 2  # own lease expired: a new lease, a new token


def test_release_boundaries_and_preconditions():
    _, svc = make()
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    assert svc.release("a", 1, TTL) is False  # expired exactly at ttl
    assert svc.acquire("a", 1) == 1  # failed release changed nothing
    assert svc.release("b", 1, 1) is False  # wrong client only
    assert svc.release("a", 2, 1) is False  # wrong token only
    assert svc.release("a", 0, 1) is False
    assert svc.acquire("b", 1) is None  # still held
    assert svc.release("a", 1, TTL - 1) is True


def test_release_of_stale_lease_does_not_free_new_one():
    _, svc = make()
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    assert svc.acquire("b", 5) == 2
    assert svc.release("a", 1, 5) is False
    assert svc.acquire("c", 5) is None


def test_tokens_strictly_increase_across_release_and_expiry():
    _, svc = make()
    seen = []
    for i in range(5):
        seen.append(svc.acquire("a", 10 * i))
        if i % 2:
            svc.release("a", seen[-1], 10 * i)
    assert seen == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]


def test_out_of_order_times():
    _, svc = make()
    assert svc.acquire("a", 10) == 1  # lease until 12
    assert svc.acquire("b", 5) is None  # earlier time: lease unexpired
    assert svc.release("a", 1, 3) is True  # unexpired at 3 too
    assert svc.acquire("b", 3) == 2
    assert svc.acquire("a", 4) is None  # b holds until 5
    assert svc.acquire("a", 5) == 3


def test_state_lives_in_store_not_objects():
    store = Store()
    s1, s2 = LockService(store, TTL), LockService(store, TTL)
    assert s1.acquire("a", 0) == 1
    assert s2.acquire("b", 0) is None
    assert s2.acquire("a", 0) == 1
    assert s2.release("a", 1, 0) is True
    assert s1.acquire("b", 0) == 2
    assert LockService(store, TTL).acquire("c", 0) is None


# ---- fencing -----------------------------------------------------------------

def test_write_fencing_rules():
    store, svc = make()
    r = Resource(store, "r")
    assert r.read() is None
    assert r.write(1, "x") is False  # never issued
    assert r.read() is None
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    svc.acquire("b", 2)
    svc.acquire("a", 4)  # tokens 1..3 issued
    assert r.write(0, "z") is False
    assert r.write(-1, "z") is False
    assert r.write(4, "z") is False  # never issued
    assert r.write(2, "two") is True
    assert r.write(2, "two-again") is True  # equal token is not lower
    assert r.write(1, "one") is False  # lower than accepted
    assert r.read() == "two-again"
    assert r.write(3, "three") is True
    assert r.write(2, "late") is False
    assert r.read() == "three"
    assert r.write(5, "future") is False
    assert r.read() == "three"


def test_fencing_is_independent_per_resource_and_shared_via_store():
    store, svc = make()
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    svc.acquire("b", 2)
    r1, r2, r1b = Resource(store, "r1"), Resource(store, "r2"), Resource(store, "r1")
    assert r1.write(2, "x") is True
    assert r2.write(1, "y") is True  # r2 has seen nothing higher
    assert r1b.write(1, "stale") is False  # another object, same name, same store
    assert r1b.read() == "x" and r2.read() == "y"


def test_resource_name_does_not_collide_with_lock():
    store, svc = make()
    r = Resource(store, "lock")
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    assert r.write(1, "v") is True
    assert svc.acquire("a", 1) == 1 and svc.release("a", 1, 1) is True


def test_stale_holder_is_fenced_after_takeover():
    store, svc = make()
    r = Resource(store, "r")
    t1 = svc.acquire("a", 0)
    t2 = svc.acquire("b", 5)
    assert r.write(t2, "b-data") is True
    assert r.write(t1, "a-late") is False
    assert r.read() == "b-data"


# ---- forced interleavings (scenarios from the model) ---------------------------

def test_two_acquirers_read_same_version():
    inner = Store()
    barrier = threading.Barrier(2, timeout=5)
    store = HookStore(inner)
    store.after_load("lock", 1, barrier.wait)
    store.after_load("lock", 2, barrier.wait)
    results = {}

    def go(name):
        results[name] = LockService(store, TTL).acquire(name, 0)

    ts = [threading.Thread(target=go, args=(n,)) for n in "ab"]
    [t.start() for t in ts]
    [t.join(10) for t in ts]
    assert sorted(results.values(), key=lambda v: (v is None, v)) == [1, None]
    # state afterwards: exactly one holder, next token is 2
    winner = next(n for n, v in results.items() if v == 1)
    assert LockService(inner, TTL).acquire(winner, 1) == 1


def test_competitor_between_load_and_cas_in_acquire():
    inner = Store()
    store = HookStore(inner)
    other = LockService(inner, TTL)
    store.after_load("lock", 1, lambda: other.acquire("b", 0))
    assert LockService(store, TTL).acquire("a", 0) is None  # must re-decide, not overwrite b
    assert other.acquire("b", 1) == 1


def test_competitor_between_load_and_cas_same_client_gets_same_token():
    inner = Store()
    store = HookStore(inner)
    other = LockService(inner, TTL)
    store.after_load("lock", 1, lambda: other.acquire("a", 0))
    assert LockService(store, TTL).acquire("a", 0) == 1  # not a second token
    assert other.acquire("b", 1) is None


def test_release_races_with_expiry_and_takeover():
    inner = Store()
    svc = LockService(inner, TTL)
    store = HookStore(inner)
    assert svc.acquire("a", 0) == 1
    store.after_load("lock", 1, lambda: svc.acquire("b", TTL))  # a's lease expired, b took over
    assert LockService(store, TTL).release("a", 1, 1) is False  # stale decision must not free b
    assert svc.acquire("c", TTL) is None


def test_double_release_race():
    inner = Store()
    svc = LockService(inner, TTL)
    store = HookStore(inner)
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    store.after_load("lock", 1, lambda: svc.release("a", 1, 0))
    assert LockService(store, TTL).release("a", 1, 0) is False  # exactly one release wins
    assert svc.acquire("b", 0) == 2


def test_release_races_with_reacquire_by_holder():
    inner = Store()
    svc = LockService(inner, TTL)
    store = HookStore(inner)
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    # a's own release (time 1) decides from stale state while a releases and re-acquires.
    def competitor():
        svc.release("a", 1, 1)
        assert svc.acquire("a", 1) == 2
    store.after_load("lock", 1, competitor)
    assert LockService(store, TTL).release("a", 1, 1) is False  # token 1 is gone
    assert svc.release("a", 2, 1) is True


def test_stale_write_cas_must_retry_not_lower_max():
    inner = Store()
    svc = LockService(inner, TTL)
    for i, who in enumerate("aba"):
        svc.acquire(who, 2 * i)  # tokens 1, 2, 3
    store = HookStore(inner)
    fast = Resource(inner, "r")
    slow = Resource(store, "r")
    store.after_load("res:r", 1, lambda: fast.write(3, "three"))
    assert slow.write(1, "one") is False  # loaded max 0, then 3 landed
    assert slow.write(2, "two") is False  # max must still be 3
    assert fast.read() == "three"


def test_concurrent_equal_and_higher_writes_keep_highest():
    inner = Store()
    svc = LockService(inner, TTL)
    for i, who in enumerate("abc"):
        svc.acquire(who, 2 * i)
    store = HookStore(inner)
    slow = Resource(store, "r")
    fast = Resource(inner, "r")
    store.after_load("res:r", 1, lambda: fast.write(2, "two"))
    assert slow.write(2, "slow-two") is True  # equal token still allowed after retry
    assert slow.write(1, "x") is False
    assert slow.write(3, "three") is True
    assert fast.read() == "three"


def test_token_issued_while_write_in_flight_is_accepted():
    inner = Store()
    svc = LockService(inner, TTL)
    svc.acquire("a", 0)
    res = Resource(inner, "r")
    assert res.write(2, "early") is False  # not issued yet
    svc.acquire("b", 2)
    assert res.write(2, "now") is True


def test_thread_stress_unique_increasing_tokens_and_fenced_writes():
    store = Store()
    granted = []
    glock = threading.Lock()

    def worker(name):
        svc = LockService(store, TTL)
        res = Resource(store, "r")
        for now in range(0, 60, 2):
            t = svc.acquire(name, now)
            if t is not None:
                with glock:
                    granted.append((now, t, name))
                res.write(t, name)

    ts = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(f"c{i}",)) for i in range(6)]
    [t.start() for t in ts]
    [t.join(30) for t in ts]
    tokens = [t for _, t, _ in granted]
    assert all(t >= 1 for t in tokens)
    # One token per lease: leases never share a token between different clients.
    by_token = {}
    for _, t, n in granted:
        by_token.setdefault(t, set()).add(n)
    assert all(len(v) == 1 for v in by_token.values())
    # The last lease issued matches the resource's accepted maximum.
    final = LockService(store, TTL).acquire("zz", 1000)
    assert final == max(tokens) + 1


# ---- observation against the P spec --------------------------------------------

def test_observed_history_matches_p_spec():
    store, svc = make()
    res = Resource(store, "r")
    ids = {"a": 1, "b": 2}
    events = []

    def acquire(c, now):
        events.append({"event": "eInvoked", "payload": {"cid": ids[c], "kind": 0, "now": now, "tok": 0}})
        tok = svc.acquire(c, now)
        events.append({"event": "eAcq", "payload": {"cid": ids[c], "now": now, "token": tok or 0}})

    def release(c, tok, now):
        events.append({"event": "eInvoked", "payload": {"cid": ids[c], "kind": 1, "now": now, "tok": tok}})
        ok = svc.release(c, tok, now)
        events.append({"event": "eRel", "payload": {"cid": ids[c], "token": tok, "now": now, "ok": ok}})

    def write(c, tok):
        events.append({"event": "eInvoked", "payload": {"cid": ids[c], "kind": 2, "now": 0, "tok": tok}})
        ok = res.write(tok, "v")
        events.append({"event": "eWrote", "payload": {"cid": ids[c], "token": tok, "ok": ok}})

    acquire("a", 0)
    acquire("b", 1)
    acquire("a", 1)
    write("a", 1)
    write("a", 7)
    release("b", 1, 1)
    release("a", 1, 1)
    acquire("b", 1)
    write("b", 2)
    write("a", 1)
    write("b", 2)
    release("b", 2, 3)
    acquire("a", 3)
    write("a", 3)
    release("a", 3, 5)
    events.append({"event": "eDone", "payload": sum(e["event"] != "eInvoked" for e in events)})
    check_events(events, "LockContract", spec_files=["Lock.p"], strict=True)


def test_spec_rejects_a_wrong_history():
    events = [
        {"event": "eInvoked", "payload": {"cid": 1, "kind": 0, "now": 0, "tok": 0}},
        {"event": "eAcq", "payload": {"cid": 1, "now": 0, "token": 1}},
        {"event": "eInvoked", "payload": {"cid": 2, "kind": 0, "now": 1, "tok": 0}},
        {"event": "eAcq", "payload": {"cid": 2, "now": 1, "token": 2}},  # lease still held
    ]
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        check_events(events, "LockContract", spec_files=["Lock.p"], strict=True)

# Lock service with fencing tokens

Files: `solution.py` (implementation), `Lock.p` + `Lock.pproj` (P model and `LockContract`
spec), `test_solution.py` (pytest). Run `snappea check` and `python -m pytest`.

## Contract
- `acquire(c, now)`: if no unexpired lease, grant a new lease expiring at `now + ttl` with token
  `last_issued + 1`; if `c` holds the unexpired lease, return its token; otherwise `None`.
  Unexpired means `now < expires`; at `now == expires` it is expired. Any `now` order is allowed.
- `release(c, t, now)`: True only if `c` holds the lease with token `t` and `now < expires`
  (then the lease ends); otherwise False with no effect.
- Tokens strictly increase for the life of the store, across release and expiry.
- `Resource.write(t, v)`: False with no effect if `t` was never issued (`t < 1` or `t > last`)
  or `t` < highest token of an accepted write to this resource; otherwise stores and True
  (an equal token is accepted).

## Primitives
Only per-key `load` and `compare_swap`. No cross-key atomicity. Two keys:
- `"lock"`: `{last, holder, token, expires}` (`last` = highest issued token; it always equals
  `token`, so `last` is kept only for clarity).
- `"res:<name>"`: `{max, value}`.
Every state change is one CAS on one key, retried after reload on failure. Read-only outcomes
(refusal, own-token return, failed release, rejected write) are linearized at the load.
Write checks issuance on the lock key and the fence on the resource key as two separate steps.
This is safe because `last` only grows (an issued token stays issued), and `max` only grows
(a token below `max` stays rejected).

## Scenarios (each is a P test and/or pytest)
1. Two acquirers read the same version (one CAS fails and must re-decide): `GenAcq`, barrier test.
2. Competitor acquires between load and CAS; same client's competitor must not create a second
   token: competitor tests.
3. Release racing with expiry + takeover, with double release, and with release + re-acquire.
4. Boundaries: `now == expires` for acquire and release; ttl off-by-one; out-of-order times.
5. Stale holder fenced after takeover; unissued token (0, negative, `last+1`); equal token.
6. Lost update on the resource: write(1) loads max 0, write(3) lands, write(1)'s CAS must fail,
   then write(2) must still be rejected: `RaceWrite`, `test_stale_write_cas_must_retry_not_lower_max`.
7. Two objects (and two names) sharing a store; resource key not colliding with the lock key.

## Model (`Lock.p`)
`Store` holds both records with load and CAS. `Client` loads, decides from the snapshot only,
and sends a candidate plus the result; the store commits it only at the expected version.
`LockContract` recomputes every result from the request history (it does not read the store)
and checks that each result belongs to the invoked operation. Tests: `tcFixed`, `tcGenLock`,
`tcGenAcq`, `tcGenWrite`, `tcStale`, `tcExpiry`, `tcSerialRelease`, `tcSerialTakeover`,
`tcRaceWrite`. Bounds: ttl 2, 2-3 clients (client 3 only issues tokens first), at most 4-7
operations in total, times 0..4, tokens 0..4, at most 4 CAS attempts per call. Searches are
complete for those bounds. `snappea check` passes with coverage and mutation checks; 0 mutants
undetected, a few equivalent ones suppressed with a reason in `Lock.p`.

## What the model found
My first model let the store recompute the decision at CAS time; that hid every stale-snapshot
bug (surviving mutants: version never bumped, version check ignored). I moved the decision into
the client and added `RaceWrite` (tokens issued first, then the racing writes): without the
version bump it fails. Mutation checks also showed the oracle did not tie results to the invoked
operation, so `eInvoked` was added.

## Implementation checks
`test_solution.py` forces interleavings with a store wrapper (a competing call between load and
CAS, a barrier so two calls read the same version), replays through second objects, tests
boundaries, runs thread stress, and checks a real recorded history against `LockContract` with
`snappea.check_events` (plus a wrong history that must be rejected).
Hand-made breaks that all fail a test: ignoring each CAS result; `<` to `<=` for acquire,
release, and the fence; dropping the expiry, client, or token check on release; skipping the
issued check or off-by-one on it; resetting `last` on release; not returning the own token;
ttl off by one; shared resource key / key collision with the lock; no retry on a stale write
CAS; a stale cached lock read; `max` kept in the object instead of the store.
One break survives and is equivalent: computing the next token from `token` instead of `last`
(they are always equal).

## Not covered
Crashes between steps, store failures, a clock that is not caller-supplied, non-int tokens or
non-string clients (clients only need equality), more than 3 clients, tokens beyond the model's
range, and fairness or liveness under unbounded contention (the retry loop has no cap).
Observation checks only sequential histories; thread stress uses plain assertions.
